title: Metric name guardrails and span semantic playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic playbook for onboarding new metrics and spans into our observability stack. Focus: consistent metric naming, minimal but sufficient span semantics for inference request paths, and mapping those signals into dashboard widgets that are easy for oncall and platform teams to use.

Why this exists (short):
- We repeatedly get inconsistencies: e.g., two teams emitting `inference.latency` with different units and different tags.
- Dashboards become brittle and expensive when downstream queries assume specific tag sets or cardinality.
- Traces with overloaded span names make root cause hunting slower ("model_call" used for both KV-cache warm and cold runs).

Quick rules (aka guardrails):
1) Metric names: dot-separated, stable root, and semantic suffixes.
   - Root namespace: `redwood.` (internal) or `customer.` (customer-facing cost signals)
   - Service context: `inference`, `kvcache`, `batcher`, `router`, `auth`
   - Measurement suffix: `._count`, `._latency_ms`, `._size_bytes`, `._gauge`, `._ratio`
   - Example: `redwood.inference.request_latency_ms` (histogram/summary), `redwood.kvcache.hit_ratio` (ratio)

2) Units and types: always include unit in name (ms, bytes, count). Metric type must be explicit in registration (counter/gauge/histogram).
   - Counters: use `_count` suffix and monotonically increasing semantics.
   - Histograms: use `_latency_ms` suffix; tag with `quantiles` at query time, not on ingestion.

3) Tags/labels: minimal set. Each metric may include up to these tags: `env`, `region`, `team`, `model`, `model_variant`, `route`, `tenant_id` (if multi-tenant).
   - Avoid high-cardinality tags like `user_id`, `session_id` on ingest; only attach in spans or sample traces.
   - When a tag is optional (e.g., model_variant) and missing, emit `model_variant:unknown` to keep cardinality stable.

4) Naming conventions for spans: verbs-first, semantic anchors, and explicit event annotations.
   - Span name pattern: `<component>.<operation>` e.g., `kvcache.lookup`, `inference.decode`, `router.route_evaluate`.
   - Add span attribute keys for mutable context (no more than a handful): `tenant.id`, `model.name`, `request.id`, `seq_len`, `batch_size`, `hardware.type`.
   - Annotate special events (cache_miss, fallback_triggered) as attributes not as separate span types to avoid explosion in span types.

Span semantics: short primer
- Root span: `request.dispatch` (represents the full external request lifecycle). Attach high-level fields: `route`, `client_api_key_hash`, `priority_tier`.
- Child spans should be narrow in scope: `router.evaluate` (routing decision), `model.load` (model weight fetch), `inference.forward`, `inference.decode`, `kvcache.lookup`, `kvcache.store`, `batcher.wait`.
- Synchronous vs async: include `async` attribute true/false for spans that run on separate worker processes.

Example span attribute mapping (what to include):
- request.dispatch: {request.id, tenant.id, route, input_tokens, output_tokens_estimate, start_timestamp}
- router.evaluate: {candidate_models, selected_model, fallback_reason?}
- kvcache.lookup: {cache_key_type, hit:boolean, latency_ms}
- inference.forward: {model.name, model_variant, sequence_length, hardware.type, latency_ms}

Dashboard mapping notes (how to turn metrics/spans into practical widgets):
- Health panel: aggregated error rate by `route` and `model` (use `redwood.inference.error_count / redwood.inference.request_count`). Show last 1h, 6h, 24h.
- Latency heatmap: use bucketed histograms from `_latency_ms` grouped by `route` and `tenant_id` (with sample size filtering).
- Cache warmth panel: `kvcache.hit_ratio` by model and by region; tie this to a small sparkline for last 24h and a top-10 lowest-warmth list.
- Cost-attribution: token counts per model (`redwood.inference.tokens_input_count`, `redwood.inference.tokens_output_count`) with per-model token cost estimate.
- Trace link button: every dashboard row should include a quick link to sample traces filtered by `request.id` or `route` to jump into detailed root cause.

Onboarding checklist for a new metric/span (practical):
- [ ] Draft name + unit + type + allowed tags in a one-line PR description.
- [ ] Create a single-line Confluence entry in the metric catalog (title, owner, description, example query, linked dashboards, expected cardinality).
- [ ] Add assertion tests in CI: sanity of type and a smoke query that runs during deploys (e.g., registers metric exists and is non-empty over last 24h in staging).
- [ ] Add a dashboard widget wireframe in a shared Grafana/Looker repo and link it in the catalog entry.
- [ ] Add a short note in the rollout playbook: fallback behavior if metric missing or mis-typed.

Dashboard layout heuristics (practical operator-first):
- Top row: availability + error budget. Second row: latency Q50/Q95/Q99. Third row: capacity signals (cpu/gpu/queue depth). Fourth row: quality signals (hallucination metric if available) + session-level traces anchor.
- Keep each panel query <500ms (pre-aggregations where possible). Prefer precomputed aggregation metrics for high-cardinality joins.

Cardinality & cost mitigation:
- If a metric is high-cardinality by model+route+tenant, pre-aggregate by `model` and `route` at ingestion and emit `*_by_model_route` metrics rather than full-dimension raw events.
- Use sampling for traces (adaptive sampling weights for error traces x10, normal traces x0.01). Document sampling policy in metric catalog entry.

Operator / oncall quick-card (two-sentence cheats):
- If latency spikes: check cache warmth, batcher.queue_depth, and recent routing fallbacks. Quick queries: `redwood.kvcache.hit_ratio` and `redwood.batcher.queue_depth_gauge` by region.
- If error rate increases: find a top failing `route`, then click to sample traces to identify model or infra cause.

Open questions / tradeoffs we should decide in next sync:
- Do we require `tenant_id` on all request metrics for multi-tenant billing? (cost vs cardinality)
- Standardize a single histogram library (client-side vs server-side) to ensure consistent bucket boundaries for latency MS.
- Naming for function/tool-invocations (tool.call vs tool.invoke): unify to one canonical verb.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Marisol: draft a short RFC for `tenant_id` ingestion policy (due 2024-11-15).
- Tom: add CI assertion template to observability repo (PR #725, due 2024-11-08).
- Priya: draft pre-aggregation cookbook for high-cardinality metrics (first pass: 2024-11-01).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the playbook short; prefer examples and checklists. Avoid perfect taxonomy now — we need practical enforcement (CI + dashboards) first.
- When in doubt, prefer an explicit unknown tag value than absent label.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: Metric Catalog v2 (see linked_artifacts above)
- Slack thread: #obs-metrics (search "naming inconsistency 2024-08")
- Existing tickets: JIRA-OBS-4823 (dashboard rewrite), JIRA-OBS-4950 (adaptive trace sampler)

End of doc.
